chunks: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Mukattib narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Tayyib Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Warraq narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Durayd al-Azdi al-Umani narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas ibn al-Faraj al-Riyashi narrated to us. He said: Abu Zayd al-Nahwi al-Ansari narrated to me. He said: I asked al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Arudi,

and said: Why did the people abandon Ali (peace be upon him), when his closeness to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) was such, and his position among the Muslims was such, and his striving for Islam was such?

So he said: By God, his light dazzled their lights, and he surpassed them at the choicest part of every watering place, and people incline more toward those who resemble them. Have you not heard the first poet when he says: "Every sort inclines toward its own sort. Do you not see the elephant befriends elephants?"

He said: And al-Riyashi recited to us, regarding this same meaning, from al-Abbas ibn al-Ahnaf: "A questioner says: How did you two part? So I gave a reply that was fair. He was not of my sort, so I left him. People are of various sorts and inclinations."

key_terms.آلف: One who is fond of, inclined toward — from the root ألف meaning familiarity and affection
key_terms.أشكال: Sorts, kinds, types — referring to the principle that like associates with like
key_terms.منهل: Watering place — metaphor for any field of merit or distinction

ai.seo_question: Why did people abandon Imam Ali according to al-Khalil ibn Ahmad?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Amali of al-Saduq records the famous grammarian al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi's explanation for why people distanced themselves from Imam Ali (AS). When asked by Abu Zayd al-Ansari why people abandoned Ali despite his kinship to the Prophet, his standing among Muslims, and his sacrifices for Islam, al-Khalil answered that Ali's light outshone theirs, and people naturally gravitate toward their own kind. He supported his point with two Arabic poems affirming that like seeks like.
